name: The First Martyrs of the Holy Roman Church
history: The unnamed Christians of Rome put to death by Nero after the great fire of July 64, which he blamed on them. The Roman historian Tacitus, no friend of the faith, records their deaths with something like pity. The day after Peter and Paul, the Church honours this great multitude who died with the apostles.
life: In July 64 a fire swept through Rome for nearly a week and destroyed much of the city. Rumour held that the Emperor Nero had started it, and to deflect the blame he turned on the Christians, a small and despised community. Tacitus, writing some fifty years later, says that a vast number were convicted, not so much of arson as of hatred of the human race. Some were dressed in the skins of animals and torn by dogs, some crucified, and some set alight to serve as torches in Nero’s gardens, near the Vatican Hill, while he drove among the crowds in a charioteer’s dress. Saint Clement of Rome, writing to the Corinthians at the end of the century, remembers this great multitude of the elect alongside Peter and Paul. Their names are lost, but their blood was, in Tertullian’s phrase, the seed of Christians.
prayerTo: Holy martyrs of Rome, you died nameless and despised, and God has written your names in heaven. Pray for Christians persecuted today, for those blamed for what they did not do, and for me, that I may not be ashamed of Christ when the world turns against Him. Amen.
penance: Find out about one country where Christians are persecuted now, pray for them, and give to a charity that helps them.
meditation: We do not know a single one of their names. Can you be content to serve God unknown?
